facts.label: Credit analysis by dimension
facts.text: Leverage is a story about the denominator. Calculated reported EBITDA was negative in FY2024 (negative USD 169.212 million) and FY2025 (negative USD 82.898 million) and on a last-twelve-months basis to March and June 2026, so no leverage ratio can be stated for those dates. Last-twelve-months EBITDA at September 2026 was USD 37.048 million; the third quarter alone contributed USD 40.801 million, while the other three quarters of the window sum to negative USD 3.753 million. Debt rose by USD 40.136 million in the third quarter to USD 164.062 million of carrying value as the revolver was drawn, which gives total debt of 4.43x and net debt of 2.24x EBITDA. A creditor should read these ratios as resting on one quarter, not on a trend. Basis: calculation CALC-03; calculation CALC-06; calculation CALC-10; calculation CALC-13; 10-Q_2026-09-30_mxl-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 4–5, 19

facts.label: Credit analysis by dimension
facts.text: Cash generation lags earnings. Operating cash flow was negative USD 17.653 million in the first nine months of 2026 against positive USD 9.213 million a year earlier, although operating income swung from a loss of USD 111.998 million to a profit of USD 8.833 million. The company attributes about USD 137.6 million of working-capital investment to wafer prepayments and inventory; prepaid expenses and other current assets rose from USD 50.390 million to USD 121.648 million and inventory from USD 78.104 million to USD 113.722 million between December 2025 and September 2026, and inventory purchase and other contractual obligations rose from USD 209.6 million to USD 347.6 million. After capital expenditure of USD 15.035 million, free cash flow for the nine months was negative USD 32.688 million. Growth is being pre-funded: if orders slowed, the company would hold inventory and prepayments it has committed to pay for while the revolver carried the gap. Basis: calculation CALC-08; 10-Q_2026-09-30_mxl-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 4, 6, 59, 62

The company attributes about USD 137.6 million of working-capital investment to wafer prepayments and inventory; prepaid expenses and other current assets rose from USD 50.390 million to USD 121.648 million and inventory from USD 78.104 million to USD 113.722 million between December 2025 and September 2026, and inventory purchase and other contractual obligations rose from USD 209.6 million to USD 347.6 million. After capital expenditure of USD 15.035 million, free cash flow for the nine months was negative USD 32.688 million. Growth is being pre-funded: if orders slowed, the company would hold inventory and prepayments it has committed to pay for while the revolver carried the gap.
Basis: calculation CALC-08; 10-Q_2026-09-30_mxl-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 4, 6, 59, 62

facts.label: Credit analysis by dimension
facts.text: EBITDA is the weakest figure in this foundation. The company states none, the calculated measure includes right-of-use amortization of USD 5.336 million for the nine months of 2026 (USD 5.632 million a year earlier) because the annual report and first-quarter report print one combined line, and the credit agreement's Consolidated EBITDA, which governs the 3.50x total net leverage covenant, is not supplied. Net leverage of 2.24x on the calculated measure is therefore not covenant headroom. The liquidity covenant is described three ways across the 2026 filings: a minimum of USD 80 million in the first-quarter and third-quarter reports, a ceiling of 100% of Consolidated EBITDA in the second-quarter debt note and a minimum of USD 80 million again in the second-quarter liquidity discussion, while the annual report describes only a springing secured net leverage test. facts.label: Credit analysis by dimension
facts.text: The strongest case against caution is breadth. Revenue of USD 218.057 million in the third quarter was 72.43% above the prior-year quarter, gross margin was 58.73%, operating margin was 13.86%, infrastructure revenue reached 57.28% of the total, no customer reached 10% of revenue in the quarter, and management guided fourth-quarter revenue to USD 240 million to USD 260 million. If the fourth quarter delivers that range, last-twelve-months EBITDA rises and leverage falls without any change in debt. The view would change in favour of creditors after two more quarters of EBITDA near the third-quarter level together with positive operating cash flow, and against them on a revenue miss, an inventory write-down or a further revolver draw to meet purchase commitments. Basis: calculation CALC-11; 10-Q_2026-09-30_mxl-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 33–35; EX-99.1_2026-10-22_a09302026exhibit991.htm.jsonl, page 2

facts.basis: Literal handoff table; no financial reinterpretation.

facts.text: Revenue durability is average: growth is fast but rests on a narrow group of data center programs and on customers who buy without long-term commitments. Revenue rose 58.24% to USD 524.1 million in the first nine months of 2026, infrastructure became 52% of sales from 31% a year earlier, and the ten largest customers were 56% of revenue, yet revenue fell 48.00% in 2024 before it recovered, so the cycle can reverse as fast as it rose. facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: Margin resilience is average: gross margin is high and steady, but operating profit depends on revenue staying above a large fixed cost base. A larger fall would return the company to operating losses, as in 2025 when the operating margin was -27.13%. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_mxl-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 4–5, 51–53; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation CALC-04; calculation CALC-05

facts.text: Liquidity is adequate and no debt falls due before 2028, but the buffer is thin against commitments and depends on the revolver. facts.label: Business, ownership and revenue durability
facts.text: MaxLinear designs communications chips and outsources all manufacturing, so its revenue depends on winning design slots at a few large customers rather than on owned capacity. The infrastructure line, which management ties to optical products for data centers, high-performance analog and wireless backhaul, was 57% of third-quarter revenue, broadband fell as customers moved to a new standard, and the company reports one operating segment. Product life cycles of 24 to 60 months give some visibility once a design is won, but customers buy on purchase orders, distributors were 48% of third-quarter revenue, the company carries accrued price protection of USD 30,367 thousand, and price changes had no material effect on revenue. Revenue is therefore cyclical and concentrated, not contractual, and supports debt service only while data center demand lasts. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_mxl-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 8, 34–36, 46–47, 50–51; Business & governance (CP-1A)

facts.label: Competitive and macro forces
facts.text: Competitive rivalry is intense: the annual report names thirteen merchant semiconductor competitors including Broadcom, Marvell, Credo and MediaTek, several far larger, and notes that some module makers supply components in house. Buyer power is high, with the ten largest customers at 56% of revenue and one customer at 10%; supplier power is high too, with one supplier at 54% of inventory purchases, key foundries in Taiwan and prepayments that tie cash to wafer capacity. Entry and substitution threats are lower in the near term because design wins take long to move, but customers can develop their own products or adopt a competitor's. Each force bears on the same creditor outcome: gross margin and cash conversion in a downturn. facts.label: Competitive and macro forces
facts.text: Trade and geopolitical factors are material, so the PEST view applies. Export controls have already led the company to restrict or curtail business with certain customers and partners in China, demand in China has weakened, tariffs could pressure average selling prices as customers offset their own costs, and Taiwan-China developments could affect supply from Taiwan, where key foundry capacity sits. Shipments to Asia were 85% of nine-month revenue, so a trade or export-control shock would hit volume and supply together; the Singapore tax incentive runs only to March 2027, a modest cash tax risk. facts.label: Downside scenario
facts.text: The scenario starts with a hyperscale customer pausing or re-sequencing optical data center orders, which management names as a risk. The first operational break is inventory and commitments: USD 272,967 thousand of inventory purchase obligations, USD 113,722 thousand of inventory and USD 121,648 thousand of prepaid and other current assets are already placed against forecast demand, and firm orders go to suppliers up to 26 weeks ahead. Revenue then falls, gross margin falls on write-downs and the third-quarter cost base of USD 97,843 thousand is not cut quickly, so operating income turns negative below about USD 166,591 thousand of quarterly revenue and cash is consumed by commitments. The liquidity consequence is a draw on the revolver: headroom of USD 91,085 thousand over the USD 80.0 million covenant minimum would last about 5.30 quarters at the 2024 burn rate and about 8.36 quarters at the 2026 nine-month burn rate, before any Silicon Motion payment. The observable triggers are quarterly revenue below USD 166,591 thousand, a rising price protection liability, further revolver drawings and cash plus availability approaching the covenant minimum. Resilience appears sufficient to avoid liquidity distress within 12 to 24 months absent a large claim payment, but not to refinance comfortably in 2028 without a recovery in EBITDA. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_mxl-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 4, 22–24, 36, 37, 59; EX-99.1_2026-10-22_a09302026exhibit991.htm.jsonl, page 3; 10-K_2025-12-31_mxl-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 22, 82; calculation CALC-05; calculation CALC-11

facts.label: Overall credit view
facts.text: Overall, MAXLINEAR, INC presents an adequate but unproven business profile supported by a data center-led growth inflection, low capital intensity, no sponsor and no debt due before 2028, but credit quality is constrained by negative cash conversion, customer and supplier concentration and an unpriced Silicon Motion claim. Cash-flow durability appears weak until working capital releases and EBITDA is repeated. Refinancing capacity is likely to depend on sustaining positive EBITDA through 2027, on the revolver remaining available and on the claim not requiring debt. The primary downside path is a hyperscale order pause that strands supply commitments while the fixed cost base stays. Further analysis would require the executed credit agreement, the proxy statement, ratings or dealer prices and the outcome of the arbitration. Fundamental credit analysis completed. Top risk: cash conversion under a demand pause. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); Source readiness (CP-0); calculation CALC-01; calculation CALC-06; calculation CALC-11

facts.label: Strengths and weaknesses
facts.text: The ranked strengths are as follows. First, the data center-led revenue inflection: revenue rose 58.24% in the nine months and infrastructure reached 57% of the third quarter, which lifts EBITDA and cover and supports debt service while demand lasts. Second, liquidity and maturities: USD 171,085 thousand of cash plus undrawn revolver against a covenant minimum of USD 80.0 million, and no principal due before 2028, which gives time to refinance. Third, a low-capital fabless model with a high gross margin of 58.12%, which keeps capital needs small and lets cash be directed to working capital. Fourth, conservative distribution policy with no sponsor, no dividend and a paused repurchase, which keeps cash in the business. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_mxl-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 4–6, 19–24, 34–35, 44, 50; Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation CALC-03; calculation CALC-09

## Request

MAXLINEAR, INC (issuer mxl), as of 2026-11-05, credit snapshot pathway. This answer extracts and normalises the company's financial statements, debt and liquidity from the seven supplied filings and releases and calculates leverage, cover and liquidity measures. It draws no credit conclusion beyond the data and records its gaps.

## Findings
### Bottom line

MaxLinear has moved from a deep loss to a levered recovery: last-twelve-months EBITDA turned positive only at September 2026, leaving total debt at 4.43x EBITDA, net debt at 2.24x and interest cover at 4.35x. The company states no EBITDA, so the measure is calculated here from operating income and amortization and depreciation.
Basis: calculation CALC-03; calculation CALC-06

Operating cash flow is still negative, so the recovery is being financed by revolver borrowing rather than by internal cash generation, and two secured facilities fall due in 2028 with USD 90 million of revolver commitments undrawn. Covenant headroom cannot be established because the credit agreement's EBITDA definition is not supplied.
Basis: calculation CALC-08; calculation CALC-09; 10-Q_2026-09-30_mxl-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 6, 19–24
### Credit analysis by dimension

Leverage is a story about the denominator. Calculated reported EBITDA was negative in FY2024 (negative USD 169.212 million) and FY2025 (negative USD 82.898 million) and on a last-twelve-months basis to March and June 2026, so no leverage ratio can be stated for those dates. Last-twelve-months EBITDA at September 2026 was USD 37.048 million; the third quarter alone contributed USD 40.801 million, while the other three quarters of the window sum to negative USD 3.753 million. Debt rose by USD 40.136 million in the third quarter to USD 164.062 million of carrying value as the revolver was drawn, which gives total debt of 4.43x and net debt of 2.24x EBITDA. A creditor should read these ratios as resting on one quarter, not on a trend.
Basis: calculation CALC-03; calculation CALC-06; calculation CALC-10; calculation CALC-13; 10-Q_2026-09-30_mxl-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 4–5, 19

Cover is strong on the latest quarter and moderate on a trailing basis. Last-twelve-months cash interest paid was USD 8.508 million, giving cover of 4.35x, and third-quarter EBITDA covered that quarter's cash interest of USD 2.441 million 16.71 times. Both facilities carry floating rates, with a weighted average effective rate on aggregate debt of 7.0% at September 2026, so cover is sensitive to rates and to the revolver balance. Cover was negative at every earlier date in the table because EBITDA was negative, not because interest went unpaid.
Basis: calculation CALC-04; calculation CALC-06; calculation CALC-10; 10-Q_2026-09-30_mxl-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 19

Cash generation lags earnings. Operating cash flow was negative USD 17.653 million in the first nine months of 2026 against positive USD 9.213 million a year earlier, although operating income swung from a loss of USD 111.998 million to a profit of USD 8.833 million. The company attributes about USD 137.6 million of working-capital investment to wafer prepayments and inventory; prepaid expenses and other current assets rose from USD 50.390 million to USD 121.648 million and inventory from USD 78.104 million to USD 113.722 million between December 2025 and September 2026, and inventory purchase and other contractual obligations rose from USD 209.6 million to USD 347.6 million. After capital expenditure of USD 15.035 million, free cash flow for the nine months was negative USD 32.688 million. Growth is being pre-funded: if orders slowed, the company would hold inventory and prepayments it has committed to pay for while the revolver carried the gap.
Basis: calculation CALC-08; 10-Q_2026-09-30_mxl-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 4, 6, 59, 62

Liquidity is adequate at the reporting date. Cash of USD 81.085 million and undrawn revolver commitments of USD 90.000 million total USD 171.085 million at September 2026, against a covenant minimum of USD 80 million that the October 2026 amendment cut to USD 60 million while adding USD 70 million of commitments. Both facilities mature in 2028, so no principal falls due before March 2028. Restricted cash of USD 28.779 million is excluded, and letters of credit outstanding are not stated, so availability under the revolver may be lower than shown.
Basis: calculation CALC-01; calculation CALC-09; calculation CALC-14; 10-Q_2026-09-30_mxl-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 4, 22–24, 44–45

Obligations to customers act as a non-debt funding float: the accrued price protection liability was USD 30.367 million at September 2026, against USD 26.493 million at December 2025 and USD 43.401 million at December 2024, and distributor price adjustments of USD 14.4 million sit in accrued expenses. Two items outside total debt behave like borrowing: USD 8.0 million of proceeds from selling an interest in certain claims, carried as a long-term liability, and USD 15.0 million of jointly funded research and development deferred in other long-term liabilities because repayment conditions are unresolved. Lease liabilities are carried on their own lines. None of these is added to total debt, and no adjusted figure is built.

The amendment of 16 October 2026 is kept out of every September 2026 figure. It adds USD 70 million of revolving commitments, taking total commitments to USD 200 million, and lowers the liquidity covenant minimum from USD 80 million to USD 60 million, but the filings state no borrowing under the new commitments, so net debt is unchanged. The third-quarter liquidity discussion describes the revolver as USD 200.0 million at the quarter end while the debt note puts commitments at USD 130 million at that date; this analysis uses the note's USD 130 million and treats the larger figure as the post-amendment size.
Basis: calculation CALC-14; 10-Q_2026-09-30_mxl-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 22–23, 44–45, 60

EBITDA is the weakest figure in this foundation. The company states none, the calculated measure includes right-of-use amortization of USD 5.336 million for the nine months of 2026 (USD 5.632 million a year earlier) because the annual report and first-quarter report print one combined line, and the credit agreement's Consolidated EBITDA, which governs the 3.50x total net leverage covenant, is not supplied. Net leverage of 2.24x on the calculated measure is therefore not covenant headroom. The liquidity covenant is described three ways across the 2026 filings: a minimum of USD 80 million in the first-quarter and third-quarter reports, a ceiling of 100% of Consolidated EBITDA in the second-quarter debt note and a minimum of USD 80 million again in the second-quarter liquidity discussion, while the annual report describes only a springing secured net leverage test.

Basis: calculation CALC-02; calculation CALC-12; 10-Q_2026-03-31_mxl-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 40; 10-Q_2026-06-30_mxl-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 22–24, 60; 10-Q_2026-09-30_mxl-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 23–24; 10-K_2025-12-31_mxl-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 167

The strongest case against caution is breadth. Revenue of USD 218.057 million in the third quarter was 72.43% above the prior-year quarter, gross margin was 58.73%, operating margin was 13.86%, infrastructure revenue reached 57.28% of the total, no customer reached 10% of revenue in the quarter, and management guided fourth-quarter revenue to USD 240 million to USD 260 million. If the fourth quarter delivers that range, last-twelve-months EBITDA rises and leverage falls without any change in debt. The view would change in favour of creditors after two more quarters of EBITDA near the third-quarter level together with positive operating cash flow, and against them on a revenue miss, an inventory write-down or a further revolver draw to meet purchase commitments.
Basis: calculation CALC-11; 10-Q_2026-09-30_mxl-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 33–35; EX-99.1_2026-10-22_a09302026exhibit991.htm.jsonl, page 2

The most material gaps are the missing credit agreement and amendments, which stop any covenant test, and the unquantified Silicon Motion arbitration and related suits, for which the company records no accrual and states that no loss estimate can be made. An adverse award would be an unsecured claim against the company competing for the same cash and revolver availability as debt service. Dash cells in the statements, instrument-level carrying values and the quarterly cash interest derivations are smaller limits recorded in the gap table.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_mxl-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 38–43

## Findings
### Bottom line

MaxLinear is a publicly held chip designer with no declared sponsor, so creditors face operating and litigation risk rather than owner extraction; the open exposure is an unquantified Silicon Motion damages claim that could be funded with debt. Sponsor and governance risk is medium because holder percentages, board independence and credit agreement terms are not supplied.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_mxl-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 38, 43; 10-K_2025-12-31_mxl-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 103, 127–128; Source readiness (CP-0)

Revenue grew to USD 524.1 million in the first nine months of 2026, 52% of it from the infrastructure line, but operating cash flow was an outflow of USD 17.7 million as supply commitments reached USD 347.6 million and the revolver was drawn by USD 40.0 million.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_mxl-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 4–7, 19–20, 34–35, 37, 62; calculation CALC-01; calculation CALC-02; calculation CALC-08
### Key findings

Owner-extraction risk is low on the evidence supplied: no sponsor, parent or controlling holder is named, no cash dividend has ever been declared, and the only shareholder distribution in the statements supplied, which start in 2023, was a share repurchase of USD 20.0 million in November and December 2025, in a year when free cash flow after capital spending was an outflow of USD 176 thousand and cash and restricted cash fell by USD 18,191 thousand. No repurchase followed in the first nine months of 2026, and USD 55.0 million of the USD 75.0 million authorisation remains available until November 2028. Whether the credit agreement would allow a larger distribution is not established.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_mxl-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 103–104, 137–138; 10-Q_2026-09-30_mxl-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 44, 65; calculation CALC-07

The terminated Silicon Motion merger is the transaction that matters most to creditors because its cost is still open. MaxLinear says it owed no break-up fee after terminating on July 26, 2023, while Silicon Motion seeks the termination fee plus damages in a confidential Singapore arbitration, and three suits by Silicon Motion stockholders name the company and certain officers. The company has accrued nothing and says no loss can be estimated, and its own risk disclosure warns that a payment could require drawing all lines of credit. An award would compete for the same USD 81.1 million of cash and USD 90.0 million of undrawn revolver that stand behind USD 165.0 million of debt, and the failed deal has already cost a USD 18.3 million financing ticking fee.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_mxl-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 14, 38–44, 57; 10-K_2025-12-31_mxl-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 38, 108; calculation CALC-03; calculation CALC-04

Financial policy in 2026 has favoured liquidity over distributions, at a price. The company made no repurchase and no acquisition outflow in the nine months, settled USD 32,463 thousand of bonuses in shares rather than cash, received USD 8.0 million for an interest in certain claims, and used two credit agreement amendments to push the revolver maturity to March 2028 and lift commitments from USD 100.0 million to USD 200.0 million. The revolver margin over SOFR rose to 2.25% from a range of 1.00% to 1.75%, and the October amendment cut the liquidity covenant minimum from USD 80 million to USD 60 million, a relaxation granted while the revolver was already drawn.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_mxl-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 6–7, 21–24, 44–45, 48; EX-99.1_2026-04-22_a03312026exhibit991.htm.jsonl, page 2; calculation CALC-03

The operating model is concentrated in customers, supply and geography, so one program loss or supply disruption would hit revenue and margin faster than the broad recent growth suggests. The ten largest customers were 56% of nine-month 2026 revenue (65% in 2025), one unnamed supplier provided 54% of inventory purchases (32% in 2025), 85% of revenue shipped to Asia with 50% to Hong Kong, and customers buy on purchase orders with no long-term commitments, while the company places firm orders with suppliers up to 26 weeks ahead, in some cases without a customer purchase order.

Growth is being pre-funded, which makes cash conversion the main near-term operating risk for creditors. Operating cash flow was an outflow of USD 17.7 million in the nine months because working capital absorbed approximately USD 137.6 million, mostly wafer prepayments and inventory; free cash flow after capital spending and intangible purchases was an outflow of USD 32,688 thousand; and supply and software commitments rose from USD 209.6 million to USD 347.6 million, of which USD 311,376 thousand falls due between October 2026 and December 2027 against cash plus undrawn revolver of USD 171,085 thousand. If demand slipped, the commitments and inventory would remain while revenue fell.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_mxl-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 4–7, 37, 58–59, 62; calculation CALC-05; calculation CALC-06; calculation CALC-08

Governance gives adequate reporting but little creditor-specific visibility. The statements carry an unqualified audit opinion with effective internal control, one person holds the chairman and chief executive roles with a lead director named, and the classified board and Delaware takeover provisions reduce the odds of a hostile leveraged transaction. Board independence, committee composition, executive pay and related-party dealings sit in a proxy statement that is not supplied, and the credit agreement is known only through the company's summaries, which describe the financial covenants differently across the 2026 filings, so restricted-payment, investment, debt and lien capacity cannot be tested against behavior.

Management incentives point to growth and equity value rather than creditor protection. The performance awards described vest on revenue and non-GAAP operating income, the annual report says pay is weighted to equity more heavily than at peers, most bonuses are settled in shares, and shares outstanding rose by 5.26% in nine months, so cash is conserved at the cost of dilution; none of the performance metrics described is tied to leverage or cash flow.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_mxl-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 4–5, 25–28; 10-K_2025-12-31_mxl-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 32; calculation CALC-09
### Contrary evidence and what would change the view

The strongest evidence against caution is the speed and breadth of the recovery and the company's own liquidity. Revenue of USD 168.8 million in the second quarter and USD 218.1 million in the third landed inside the outlooks of USD 160 million to USD 170 million and USD 210 million to USD 220 million that management gave a quarter earlier, the fourth-quarter outlook is USD 240 million to USD 260 million, gross margin was 58.7% in the third quarter, and infrastructure revenue grew 168% in nine months while the broadband line fell 3%. At the balance sheet date cash plus undrawn revolver of USD 171,085 thousand was well above the USD 80.0 million covenant minimum, and still above it by USD 81,085 thousand if the whole USD 10.0 million letter of credit commitment were used; the company's own fair value estimate puts the term loan at 98.72% of par, and no sponsor, dividend recapitalisation or debt-funded acquisition appears in the record.

Basis: EX-99.1_2026-04-22_a03312026exhibit991.htm.jsonl, page 2; EX-99.1_2026-07-23_a06302026exhibit991.htm.jsonl, page 1; EX-99.1_2026-10-22_a09302026exhibit991.htm.jsonl, pages 1–2; 10-Q_2026-09-30_mxl-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 20, 22–24, 50–51; calculation CALC-05; calculation CALC-10; calculation CALC-11

The view would move toward lower risk on an executed credit agreement with tight restricted-payment and investment baskets, a proxy statement showing independent directors, dispersed holdings and no related-party dealings, and a Silicon Motion settlement or award that cash on hand could fund. It would move toward higher risk on a damages award or settlement larger than available liquidity, resumed repurchases or a debt-funded acquisition while the revolver is drawn, a further covenant relaxation, the loss of a top customer, a hyperscale capital spending pullback that leaves USD 347.6 million of commitments unsupported, or an inventory write-down.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_mxl-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 37, 43, 59; Source readiness (CP-0)
### Limitations

- The proxy statement is not supplied, so board independence, committee composition, executive pay, related-party dealings and holder percentages are not established; this keeps the governance risk level at medium rather than low and leaves the low owner-extraction view resting on the absence of a named sponsor.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_mxl-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 127–128; Source readiness (CP-0)

- The executed credit agreement and its three amendments are not supplied, only the company's summaries, so capacity for restricted payments, investments, additional debt and liens is not established and willingness to extract cannot be separated from legal capacity.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_mxl-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 21–24; Source readiness (CP-0)

- Silicon Motion's termination fee and damages are not quantified and the arbitration is confidential, so the size of any payment that could be debt-funded is not established and the creditor view can change sharply on an award or settlement.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_mxl-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 38, 43

- Customers and the main supplier appear only as letters, so a concentration in a named hyperscale customer or foundry cannot be tied to a counterparty's credit standing, and the concentration finding rests on percentages alone.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_mxl-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 33–34

- No document dated after October 22, 2026 is supplied, so the outcome of the stay in the Dish action that ran to November 2, 2026, any new filing and any change in the claims against the company are not established.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_mxl-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 42, 65

- The January 2023 acquisition and the April 2020 asset purchase from Intel are named only in a contingent consideration note and the exhibit list, so their price, funding and integration record are not established and acquisition appetite is read from the absence of recent acquisition outflows, not from deal terms.

### Transaction summary and new debt issues

MaxLinear issued no new bond, note or term loan in the period covered. Its funded debt is the senior secured term B loan of USD 125.0 million due June 23, 2028, unchanged since December 2025, and borrowings of USD 40.0 million under the revolving facility of the same June 23, 2021 credit agreement, which was undrawn at the March and June quarter ends. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_mxl-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 6, 19–21; 10-Q_2026-06-30_mxl-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 6, 23; calculation CALC-04

The credit agreement was amended twice in 2026. On April 22, 2026 the revolver maturity moved from June 23, 2026 to March 23, 2028, commitments rose by USD 30.0 million to USD 130.0 million, a USD 10.0 million letter of credit commitment was added, the SOFR margin on revolver loans became 2.25% and the financial covenants became a total net leverage ratio of at most 3.50x and unrestricted cash plus undrawn commitments of at least USD 80.0 million. On October 16, 2026, after the balance sheet date, commitments rose by USD 70 million to USD 200 million and the liquidity minimum fell to USD 60 million. The effect of the October amendment on cash and borrowings is not established, because no borrowing under the new commitments is stated.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_mxl-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 22–24, 44–45, 48; EX-99.1_2026-04-22_a03312026exhibit991.htm.jsonl, page 2; calculation CALC-03

Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_mxl-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 24, 38, 59; calculation CALC-04

No acquisition is pending. The terminated Silicon Motion merger was to be financed under commitment letters with Wells Fargo and other lenders that lapsed on termination, at a cost of a USD 18.3 million ticking fee paid in August 2023, and the committed amount is not stated in the supplied documents.

The board authorised repurchases of up to USD 75.0 million on November 20, 2025; USD 20.0 million was bought by December 31, 2025 and nothing in the nine months to September 30, 2026, which leaves USD 55.0 million of authorisation. At the as-of date the revolver and the term loan mature in about 16 months and about 19 months.

# MAXLINEAR, INC (mxl): fundamental credit
## Request

MAXLINEAR, INC (issuer mxl), as of 2026-11-05, credit snapshot pathway. This answer synthesises the fundamental credit profile of MaxLinear, Inc. and its subsidiaries on a consolidated basis from the seven supplied filings and releases and the three earlier module outputs. It assigns no rating, recommendation, legal-capacity conclusion or portfolio sizing.

## Findings
### Bottom line

MaxLinear's credit profile is improving but unproven: data center demand has turned last-twelve-month EBITDA positive on one quarter, while cash flow is negative and a litigation claim is unpriced, so creditors should not yet treat the credit as stable.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation CALC-01; calculation CALC-02

At September 2026 total debt was 4.43x calculated last-twelve-months EBITDA, net debt 2.24x and cash interest cover 4.35x, with all USD 165.0 million of debt due in 2028, but that EBITDA is calculated rather than stated and the fourth-quarter outlook of USD 240 million to USD 260 million of revenue has to be met to confirm it.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_mxl-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 19–23; EX-99.1_2026-10-22_a09302026exhibit991.htm.jsonl, page 2; calculation CALC-01; calculation CALC-09
### Key findings

Revenue durability is average: growth is fast but rests on a narrow group of data center programs and on customers who buy without long-term commitments. Revenue rose 58.24% to USD 524.1 million in the first nine months of 2026, infrastructure became 52% of sales from 31% a year earlier, and the ten largest customers were 56% of revenue, yet revenue fell 48.00% in 2024 before it recovered, so the cycle can reverse as fast as it rose. Management itself lists the sustainability of hyperscale capital spending as a risk to its growth.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_mxl-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 34–36, 46–47, 50; EX-99.1_2026-10-22_a09302026exhibit991.htm.jsonl, page 3; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation CALC-03

Margin resilience is average: gross margin is high and steady, but operating profit depends on revenue staying above a large fixed cost base. Gross margin was 58.12% in the nine months against 54.03% in 2024, yet research and development alone is 32.41% of revenue, and at the third-quarter cost base operating break-even revenue is about USD 166,591 thousand a quarter, 23.60% below third-quarter revenue. A larger fall would return the company to operating losses, as in 2025 when the operating margin was -27.13%.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_mxl-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 4–5, 51–53; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation CALC-04; calculation CALC-05

Free cash flow stability is weak because earnings are not yet converting to cash. Operating cash flow was an outflow of USD 17.7 million in the nine months, and last-twelve-months free cash flow was an outflow equal to 70.09% of EBITDA, because wafer prepayments and inventory absorbed approximately USD 137.6 million and supply and software commitments rose to USD 347.6 million. The revolver, drawn by USD 40.0 million, is financing the build.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_mxl-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 6–7, 37, 59, 62; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation CALC-06

Leverage and cover are adequate on the latest quarter but unproven, because one quarter carries the recovery. Calculated last-twelve-months EBITDA of USD 37,048 thousand includes USD 40,801 thousand from the third quarter, while the other three quarters sum to negative EBITDA of USD 3,753 thousand; total debt is 4.43x and net debt 2.24x that EBITDA, and cover is 4.35x on last-twelve-months cash interest and 16.71x on the third quarter alone. Leverage would fall to about 2.00x if fourth-quarter EBITDA only matched the third quarter's at unchanged debt, and would rise sharply if it did not.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation CALC-01; calculation CALC-02; calculation CALC-07

Liquidity is adequate and no debt falls due before 2028, but the buffer is thin against commitments and depends on the revolver. Cash of USD 81.1 million plus USD 90.0 million of undrawn revolver gives USD 171,085 thousand against a covenant minimum of USD 80.0 million that falls to USD 60 million from October 2026, while purchase and software commitments of USD 311,376 thousand fall due by the end of 2027. The revolver matures in about 16 months and the term loan in about 19 months, so the 2028 refinancing needs positive EBITDA sustained through 2027; the company's own fair value estimate puts the term loan at 98.72% of par.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_mxl-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 4, 20–24, 37, 44–45, 57; calculation CALC-08; calculation CALC-09; calculation CALC-10

Financial policy and governance are average, with medium sponsor and governance risk. There is no sponsor and no dividend, and the repurchase of USD 20.0 million in late 2025 has not been repeated, but USD 55.0 million of authorisation remains, the liquidity covenant was relaxed while the revolver was drawn, and an unquantified Silicon Motion claim could be paid from the same cash and revolver that stand behind USD 165.0 million of debt.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_mxl-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 38, 43–45

The primary downside path is a pause in hyperscale optical orders that strands supply commitments while the cost base stays. It runs through USD 272,967 thousand of inventory purchase obligations and USD 121,648 thousand of prepaid and other current assets that cannot be unwound quickly, then through cash burn funded by the revolver; headroom of USD 91,085 thousand over the covenant minimum would last about 5.30 quarters at the 2024 free cash flow burn rate.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_mxl-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 4, 22–24, 37; EX-99.1_2026-10-22_a09302026exhibit991.htm.jsonl, page 3; calculation CALC-08; calculation CALC-11
### Contrary evidence and what would change the view

The strongest evidence against caution is that the third quarter may be the run rate, not a spike. Revenue of USD 168.8 million in the second quarter and USD 218.1 million in the third landed inside the outlooks of USD 160 million to USD 170 million and USD 210 million to USD 220 million that management gave a quarter earlier, the fourth-quarter outlook is 10.06% to 19.23% above third-quarter revenue, and if fourth-quarter EBITDA only equalled the third quarter's, last-twelve-months EBITDA would reach USD 81,953 thousand and total debt would be about 2.00x it. The term loan is valued at 98.72% of par by the company's own estimate and no debt is due before 2028.

Basis: EX-99.1_2026-04-22_a03312026exhibit991.htm.jsonl, page 2; EX-99.1_2026-07-23_a06302026exhibit991.htm.jsonl, page 1; EX-99.1_2026-10-22_a09302026exhibit991.htm.jsonl, pages 1–2; 10-Q_2026-09-30_mxl-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 20; calculation CALC-07; calculation CALC-10; calculation CALC-12

The view would move toward an adequate and stable credit after two more quarters of EBITDA near the third-quarter level together with positive operating cash flow, a release of wafer prepayments and inventory, and an executed credit agreement that confirms covenant headroom. It would move toward weak on fourth-quarter revenue below the USD 240 million bottom of the outlook, an inventory write-down or commitment charge, further revolver drawings that cut cash plus availability toward the covenant minimum, a Silicon Motion award or settlement larger than liquidity, or resumed repurchases while the revolver is drawn.
Basis: EX-99.1_2026-10-22_a09302026exhibit991.htm.jsonl, page 2; 10-K_2025-12-31_mxl-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 82; Business & governance (CP-1A)
### Limitations

- Profitability rests on one quarter, so the improving-profile conclusion and every leverage reading would reverse on a single weak quarter, and the fourth-quarter outlook is management's own statement, not an independent forecast.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); EX-99.1_2026-10-22_a09302026exhibit991.htm.jsonl, page 2

- EBITDA is calculated here from operating income and amortization, not stated by the company or defined by the credit agreement, so the leverage and cover ratios describe the profile but cannot show how close the company is to a covenant.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1)

- No agency rating, dealer price or peer data is supplied, so the refinancing-capacity and market-access assessments rest on the filings and on the company's own fair value estimate of the term loan, and cannot say how the market would price a new facility in 2027.
Basis: Source readiness (CP-0); 10-Q_2026-09-30_mxl-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 20

- The filings describe hyperscale demand in aggregate and say nothing about program awards, backlog or customer inventory, so the durability of the data center ramp, the main support for the revenue view, is judged from reported growth and management statements alone.
- The downside scenario is built from reported fixed costs, commitments and burn rates, not from a modelled forecast, so its timing and size show direction and not a covenant breach date.
Basis: calculation CALC-05; calculation CALC-11
### Business, ownership and revenue durability

MaxLinear designs communications chips and outsources all manufacturing, so its revenue depends on winning design slots at a few large customers rather than on owned capacity. The infrastructure line, which management ties to optical products for data centers, high-performance analog and wireless backhaul, was 57% of third-quarter revenue, broadband fell as customers moved to a new standard, and the company reports one operating segment. Product life cycles of 24 to 60 months give some visibility once a design is won, but customers buy on purchase orders, distributors were 48% of third-quarter revenue, the company carries accrued price protection of USD 30,367 thousand, and price changes had no material effect on revenue. Revenue is therefore cyclical and concentrated, not contractual, and supports debt service only while data center demand lasts.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_mxl-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 8, 34–36, 46–47, 50–51; Business & governance (CP-1A)

Ownership is public with no declared sponsor, so the credit does not carry sponsor leverage, fee or exit-pressure risk, but holder percentages and board independence are not supplied. The annual report describes a classified board and Delaware takeover provisions that make a hostile leveraged transaction harder, one person holds the chairman and chief executive roles with a lead director named, and the company has never paid a dividend. The main ownership-related exposure is the claim from the terminated Silicon Motion merger and the stockholder suits that followed it.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_mxl-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 87–88, 103, 133
### Margin resilience and cash conversion

Cost of revenue is largely variable, because wafers, assembly and test are bought from third parties, but operating expenses are fixed in the short run: research and development of USD 60,642 thousand and selling, general and administrative expense of USD 36,947 thousand in the third quarter total USD 97,843 thousand with restructuring, against gross profit of USD 128,070 thousand. That fixed base gives strong operating leverage on the way up, as the third-quarter operating margin of 13.86% against 9M 1.69% shows, and equal leverage on the way down. Margins can be defended against modest volume pressure but not against a fall of more than about a quarter in revenue, and inventory write-downs from oversupply would hit gross margin first, as the company warns.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_mxl-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 4–5, 51–54; 10-K_2025-12-31_mxl-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 82; calculation CALC-04; calculation CALC-05

Capital intensity is low, with property and equipment and intangible purchases of USD 15,035 thousand in the nine months, but working capital is the swing factor: inventory rose from USD 78,104 thousand to USD 113,722 thousand and prepaid and other current assets from USD 50,390 thousand to USD 121,648 thousand between December 2025 and September 2026, so free cash flow was an outflow of USD 32,688 thousand despite positive EBITDA. Cash interest of USD 8,508 thousand over the last twelve months is small against EBITDA, so the cash constraint is the supply build, not interest. Lease liabilities of USD 21,943 thousand and restructuring cash payments of USD 12,800 thousand in the nine months are further, smaller calls on cash.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_mxl-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 4, 6–7, 14–15, 37, 62; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation CALC-01; calculation CALC-06
### Competitive and macro forces

Competitive rivalry is intense: the annual report names thirteen merchant semiconductor competitors including Broadcom, Marvell, Credo and MediaTek, several far larger, and notes that some module makers supply components in house. Buyer power is high, with the ten largest customers at 56% of revenue and one customer at 10%; supplier power is high too, with one supplier at 54% of inventory purchases, key foundries in Taiwan and prepayments that tie cash to wafer capacity. Entry and substitution threats are lower in the near term because design wins take long to move, but customers can develop their own products or adopt a competitor's. Each force bears on the same creditor outcome: gross margin and cash conversion in a downturn.

Trade and geopolitical factors are material, so the PEST view applies. Export controls have already led the company to restrict or curtail business with certain customers and partners in China, demand in China has weakened, tariffs could pressure average selling prices as customers offset their own costs, and Taiwan-China developments could affect supply from Taiwan, where key foundry capacity sits. Shipments to Asia were 85% of nine-month revenue, so a trade or export-control shock would hit volume and supply together; the Singapore tax incentive runs only to March 2027, a modest cash tax risk.

In credit terms, the opportunities are the ramp of 800G and 1.6T optical and electrical products for AI data centers, which management says is converging with several growth drivers over the next two years, and diversification of infrastructure revenue beyond one product family. The threats are a hyperscale capital spending pullback, a competitor win at a key customer, export-control or tariff escalation and an inventory write-down; the strengths and weaknesses are ranked in the next section.
Basis: EX-99.1_2026-07-23_a06302026exhibit991.htm.jsonl, page 1; EX-99.1_2026-10-22_a09302026exhibit991.htm.jsonl, pages 1, 3
### Financial profile and credit quality

Scale is average and competitive advantage average: revenue of USD 660,528 thousand over the last twelve months is small beside the named competitors and no market share is stated, while more than one thousand patents and multi-year design-ins support incumbency but not pricing power. Business diversification is weak: there are four end markets, but customers, one supplier and one region each carry a concentration. Cost and capex flexibility is average, with low capex offset by fixed research spending and non-cancellable commitments; margin stability is average, since gross margin stayed within a 54.03% to 58.12% band across 2023 to 2026 while operating margin swung between -61.95% and 13.86%.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_mxl-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 26, 136; 10-Q_2026-09-30_mxl-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 34, 46; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation CALC-03; calculation CALC-04

Free cash flow stability is weak, liquidity position average, ability to refinance average and financial policy and governance average. Free cash flow was an outflow of USD 25,968 thousand over the last twelve months; liquidity covers the covenant minimum by USD 91,085 thousand but also covers only part of USD 347,556 thousand of commitments; refinancing in 2028 is supported by lender willingness to extend and enlarge the revolver twice in 2026 and by a term loan valued near par, but there is no rating or market issue to test access; policy is conservative on dividends and acquisitions, with an open litigation claim and unseen credit documents. Credit supports are the growth inflection, low capital intensity, no sponsor and 2028 maturities; constraints are cash conversion, concentration and one-quarter earnings; the trend is improving; missing datapoints are the credit agreement, ratings and customer identity.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_mxl-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 20, 22–24, 37; calculation CALC-06; calculation CALC-08
### Outlook, tailwinds and headwinds

For the next 12 to 24 months the company guides fourth-quarter revenue of USD 240 million to USD 260 million, so the near-term trend is growth, with margin expansion as fixed costs are spread, and EBITDA likely to stay positive if the outlook is met; tailwinds are data center optical demand and a larger revolver, headwinds are working-capital build, commitments that rose 65.84% in nine months and the unresolved litigation. Over three to five years management describes a multi-year growth phase, which is management language and not evidenced beyond the next two years; the sector is cyclical, as the 48.00% revenue fall in 2024 shows, so a medium-term credit view should assume at least one down cycle before the 2028 maturities are refinanced.

Basis: EX-99.1_2026-04-22_a03312026exhibit991.htm.jsonl, page 2; EX-99.1_2026-10-22_a09302026exhibit991.htm.jsonl, page 2; 10-K_2025-12-31_mxl-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 32; calculation CALC-03; calculation CALC-08
### Downside scenario

The scenario starts with a hyperscale customer pausing or re-sequencing optical data center orders, which management names as a risk. The first operational break is inventory and commitments: USD 272,967 thousand of inventory purchase obligations, USD 113,722 thousand of inventory and USD 121,648 thousand of prepaid and other current assets are already placed against forecast demand, and firm orders go to suppliers up to 26 weeks ahead. Revenue then falls, gross margin falls on write-downs and the third-quarter cost base of USD 97,843 thousand is not cut quickly, so operating income turns negative below about USD 166,591 thousand of quarterly revenue and cash is consumed by commitments. The liquidity consequence is a draw on the revolver: headroom of USD 91,085 thousand over the USD 80.0 million covenant minimum would last about 5.30 quarters at the 2024 burn rate and about 8.36 quarters at the 2026 nine-month burn rate, before any Silicon Motion payment. The observable triggers are quarterly revenue below USD 166,591 thousand, a rising price protection liability, further revolver drawings and cash plus availability approaching the covenant minimum. Resilience appears sufficient to avoid liquidity distress within 12 to 24 months absent a large claim payment, but not to refinance comfortably in 2028 without a recovery in EBITDA.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_mxl-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 4, 22–24, 36, 37, 59; EX-99.1_2026-10-22_a09302026exhibit991.htm.jsonl, page 3; 10-K_2025-12-31_mxl-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 22, 82; calculation CALC-05; calculation CALC-11
### Overall credit view

Overall, MAXLINEAR, INC presents an adequate but unproven business profile supported by a data center-led growth inflection, low capital intensity, no sponsor and no debt due before 2028, but credit quality is constrained by negative cash conversion, customer and supplier concentration and an unpriced Silicon Motion claim. Cash-flow durability appears weak until working capital releases and EBITDA is repeated. Refinancing capacity is likely to depend on sustaining positive EBITDA through 2027, on the revolver remaining available and on the claim not requiring debt. The primary downside path is a hyperscale order pause that strands supply commitments while the fixed cost base stays. Further analysis would require the executed credit agreement, the proxy statement, ratings or dealer prices and the outcome of the arbitration. Fundamental credit analysis completed. Top risk: cash conversion under a demand pause.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); Source readiness (CP-0); calculation CALC-01; calculation CALC-06; calculation CALC-11
### Strengths and weaknesses

The ranked strengths are as follows. First, the data center-led revenue inflection: revenue rose 58.24% in the nine months and infrastructure reached 57% of the third quarter, which lifts EBITDA and cover and supports debt service while demand lasts. Second, liquidity and maturities: USD 171,085 thousand of cash plus undrawn revolver against a covenant minimum of USD 80.0 million, and no principal due before 2028, which gives time to refinance. Third, a low-capital fabless model with a high gross margin of 58.12%, which keeps capital needs small and lets cash be directed to working capital. Fourth, conservative distribution policy with no sponsor, no dividend and a paused repurchase, which keeps cash in the business.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_mxl-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 4–6, 19–24, 34–35, 44, 50; Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation CALC-03; calculation CALC-09

The ranked weaknesses are as follows. First, negative cash conversion: operating cash flow was an outflow of USD 17.7 million and commitments reached USD 347.6 million, so growth is financed by the revolver. Second, concentration: ten customers at 56% of revenue, one supplier at 54% of purchases and 85% of shipments to Asia, which makes revenue and supply fragile to one program or trade shock. Third, recovery rests on one quarter and on calculated EBITDA, so leverage of 4.43x could look very different after one more quarter. Fourth, the Silicon Motion claim is unquantified and could compete with debt service. Fifth, covenant and document opacity: the credit agreement is known only through summaries that differ between filings, so covenant headroom and letters of credit cannot be tested.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_mxl-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 22–24, 34, 38, 43, 46, 62; Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation CALC-01; calculation CALC-06
